 Murfreesboro schools ‘secure and safe,’ under ‘precautionary lockdown’ after reported threat. Here’s what we know 
 Rutherford County Schools confirmed that Blackman Elementary, Middle and High Schools are under lockdown. 
 By Chasity Maynard Published : Nov. 10, 2026 at 12:06 PM CST | Updated : seconds ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google What This Story Is About 
 Blackman Elementary, Middle and High School were placed under lockdown Tuesday morning. 
 Why It Matters 
 The lockdowns were initiated as a precaution after the high school received a threatening phone call, according to Rutherford County Schools. 
 What Happens Next 
 Parents should not to go to the campuses right now. Instead, they should head to a reunification area at 316 Fortress Boulevard, which is the Murfreesboro Missionary Baptist Church, the sheriff’s office says. 
 For Context 
 The schools are next door to one another on Blaze Drive in Murfreesboro. 
 MURFREESBORO, Tenn. (WSMV) - Three Murfreesboro schools were placed under lockdown on Tuesday morning after receiving a phone threat, according to the school district. 
 What is the status of the lockdown?
 Rutherford County Schools confirmed to WSMV4 that Blackman Elementary, Middle and High Schools were placed under lockdown after the high school received a threatening call. The schools are next door to one another on Blaze Drive. 
 “As a precaution, we have placed the high school, the middle school and the elementary school on a precautionary lockdown while law enforcement investigates,” a spokesperson for the district said. “The scene is secure and students are safe.”
 The district spokesperson wrote in a message to parents that this response is “standard security procedure.”
 What has law enforcement said about the investigation? 
 “Initially, this appears to be what is known as a swatting call - which is a fake threat - but we always take them seriously until we have all the facts,” the district spokesperson said. 
 Parents are not able to check out their students or enter campuses during lockdown “because the campuses are secured by law enforcement.”
 “We will keep you updated as we have more information, but please know that students are safe and the scene is secure. Please do not attempt to come to campus as this will cause unneeded congestion,” the message said. 
 Sheriff’s office establishes reunification area for parents
 The Rutherford County Sheriff’s Office also asks parents not to go to the campuses right now, and instead head to a reunification area at 316 Fortress Boulevard, which is the Murfreesboro Missionary Baptist Church.
 The church is down the road from the elementary school and around the corner from the middle and high schools. 
 “Law enforcement is actively investigating. Please avoid the area at this time,” RCSO said.
